copy.name: How to test your webcam
copy.blurb: Check the preview, the real resolution and frame rate, and take a test photo. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.title: How to test your webcam
copy.lead: You have a video call coming up, or a new webcam, and want to know it works and how good it looks. You will open the camera, read what it really sends and fix the usual problems. The video stays in your browser; nothing is uploaded.
copy.result: A working preview, the camera's real resolution, aspect ratio and frame rate, and a test photo on your device.
copy.note: Video apps may lower the resolution again to save bandwidth; this test shows what the camera itself can send.
copy.s1b: Four things decide how you look on a call: resolution (720p or 1080p), frame rate (30 fps is smooth), focus and light. The test shows the first two as numbers; a photo shows the rest.
copy.s2b: Press Start camera and allow access in the prompt. You see yourself in the preview, mirrored as in a mirror; untick Mirror the preview to see what others see.
copy.s3b: With more than one camera, choose it in the Camera list. Choose 720p or 1080p in Resolution; the panel shows the size you really get, which may be lower if the camera cannot do it.
copy.s4b: Frame rate is measured from the frames actually shown. 30 fps is smooth; 15 fps or less usually means the room is too dark and the camera is exposing longer.
copy.s5t: Fix a black or missing camera
copy.s5b: Close other apps that use the camera, open the privacy shutter or press the camera key, allow camera access for the browser in system settings, and try another USB port.
copy.s6b: Press Take photo to check sharpness and colour, and Save photo to keep it. Face a window or a lamp rather than having it behind you.
copy.diagram2: Black preview: other app · shutter · permission · USB port.

faq.q1: What resolution should my webcam have?
faq.a1: 720p is fine for most calls; 1080p looks sharper when the app sends it. A 4K webcam mostly helps with cropping and zoom.
faq.a2: Clean the lens, give it light from the front, and check that the camera has focused (fixed-focus webcams are sharp from about 50 cm).
faq.a3: Low light drops the frame rate; a busy USB hub or an old USB 2.0 port can limit 1080p. Try more light, 720p or another port.
faq.a4: Yes. The video stays in your browser tab and photos are made on your device. Nothing is uploaded.
faq.a5: So moving left moves left on screen, like a mirror. Others see you unmirrored; untick Mirror the preview to see that view.

copy.name: How to test a controller and check stick drift
copy.blurb: Press every button, read both sticks and spot drift before it costs you a game. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.title: How to test a controller and check stick drift
copy.lead: Your character keeps walking on its own, or a button feels dead. You will connect the controller to the browser, test every button and trigger, and read the sticks at rest to see if they drift. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.result: Every button marked as working or not, trigger travel, both sticks' positions and a drift reading at rest.
copy.note: Games hide small drift with a dead zone, so 0.05–0.15 may not matter; it tends to grow as a stick wears.
copy.s1b: Plug it in by USB or pair it by Bluetooth. Xbox, PlayStation, Switch Pro and most generic pads work in Chrome, Edge and Firefox.
copy.s2t: Open Gamepad tester and press a button
copy.s2b: Browsers only show a controller after a button press, so press any button. The panel shows its name, layout and how many buttons and axes it has.
copy.s3b: Each button fills while held and stays outlined once it has worked. Squeeze the triggers slowly: they fill part way, showing their full travel.
copy.s4b: Move each stick around the edge, then let go. At rest it should read close to 0.00. Above 0.05 is slight drift; 0.15 or more usually shows in games.
copy.s5b: Press Test vibration. Both motors should rumble for under a second. It needs Chrome or Edge, and some Bluetooth links do not pass it through.
copy.s6b: For mild drift, raise the dead zone in the game's settings. Strong drift or a dead button usually needs cleaning, a stick module or a repair.
copy.diagram1: Standard layout: A/✕ B/○ X/□ Y/△, bumpers, triggers, sticks, D-pad.
copy.diagram2: At rest: under 0.05 fine · 0.05–0.15 slight · 0.15+ drift.

faq.a1: A stick that reports movement when nobody touches it, usually because the sensor inside has worn or picked up dirt.
faq.q2: How do I read drift in the tester?
faq.a2: Let go of the stick and read the distance under it: near 0.00 is centred, above 0.05 slight drift, 0.15 or more drift.
faq.q3: Why does my controller not show up?
faq.a3: Press a button after connecting; browsers hide controllers until then. Also close Steam's input layer or other remapping tools if they grab it.
faq.q4: Does it work with Switch Joy-Con?
faq.a4: Usually as two separate non-standard pads with numbered buttons. A Switch Pro controller shows the standard layout in most browsers.
faq.a5: No. The tester reads the controller in your browser tab with the Gamepad API.

copy.name: How to check a screen for dead pixels
copy.blurb: Show solid colours full screen and find dead, stuck or hot pixels, and tell them from dust.
copy.title: How to check a screen for dead or stuck pixels
copy.lead: You have a new monitor, laptop or phone, or bought one second-hand, and want to be sure every pixel works. You will fill the screen with solid colours and look for dots that do not change. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.result: Any dead, stuck or hot pixels found, and a clear idea whether a spot is a pixel or dust.
copy.note: Check within your return window: many shops and makers accept a screen with a set number of bad pixels only in the first days or weeks.
copy.s1t: Know the three kinds of bad pixel
copy.s1b: A dead pixel stays black (seen best on white), a stuck pixel stays red, green or blue, and a hot pixel stays white (seen best on black).
copy.s2t: Clean the screen and dim the room
copy.s2b: Wipe the screen with a dry microfibre cloth, then open Dead pixel test on cv.cm. Dim lights make small dots easier to see.
copy.s3b: Press Start full screen test. The screen turns black, then white, red, green, blue and gray as you click, press Space or →. ← goes back.
copy.s4b: Look at each colour section by section, close up, including corners and edges. Set Next colour to every 5 seconds if you want your hands free.
copy.s5b: If you see a dot, wipe the spot and look from another angle. Dust moves or blurs; a pixel stays sharp in the same place.
copy.s6b: Note where each pixel is and on which colours it shows. A stuck pixel may recover after some hours of use; a dead pixel rarely does, so use the return or warranty if it bothers you.
copy.diagram1: Dead = black dot · stuck = coloured dot · hot = white dot.
copy.diagram2: Black · white · red · green · blue · gray.

faq.q1: What is the difference between a dead and a stuck pixel?
faq.a1: A dead pixel gets no power and stays black. A stuck pixel has one or two subpixels always on, so it shows a fixed colour.
faq.q2: Can I fix a stuck pixel?
faq.a2: Sometimes it comes back after hours of normal use. Fast-flashing fixer videos exist, but they can trigger seizures and often do not help, so this test does not flash.
faq.q3: How many dead pixels are acceptable?
faq.a3: It depends on the maker's pixel policy: many allow a few on a new monitor; some promise zero. Check the warranty terms.
faq.q4: Does it work on OLED screens?
faq.a4: Yes. On OLED, also look at gray and white for burn-in: faint shapes left from static images.
faq.a5: No. The test only draws colours in your browser.

copy.name: How to check your monitor's refresh rate
copy.blurb: Measure the Hz your browser really draws at, and fix a fast screen stuck at 60 Hz.
copy.title: How to check your monitor's refresh rate (Hz)
copy.lead: You bought a 120, 144 or 240 Hz screen and want to be sure it runs that fast. You will measure the rate in the browser, read frame time and skipped frames, and check the usual settings that hold it back. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.result: Your measured refresh rate, the nearest standard rate, the frame time in ms and a count of skipped frames.
copy.note: The browser draws once per screen refresh, so this measures what you actually get, including caps from settings or power saving.
copy.s1b: Refresh rate is how many times a second the screen shows a new image. 60 Hz is a new frame every 16.7 ms, 144 Hz every 6.9 ms, 240 Hz every 4.2 ms.
copy.s2t: Open Refresh rate test on cv.cm
copy.s2b: The test starts by itself. Keep the tab in front and the window on the screen you want to test for a few seconds.
copy.s3b: The big number is the measured rate in Hz, with the nearest standard rate below. Frame time is the median time between frames.
copy.s4b: Spikes in the graph are skipped frames. Watch the moving block at different speeds: at a higher rate it moves in smaller steps and looks smoother.
copy.s5t: Fix a screen stuck at 60 Hz
copy.s5b: Set the rate in system display settings, use a cable and port that carry it (DisplayPort or HDMI 2.0+), turn off battery saver, and plug the laptop in.
copy.s6b: Press Measure again after each change. With two screens, drag the window to the other one and measure there too.
copy.diagram2: Stuck at 60: settings · cable · battery saver · screen.

faq.a1: It is accurate to the rate the browser draws at, which is the screen's rate unless something caps it. Small differences (143.9 instead of 144) are normal.
faq.q2: Why does my 144 Hz monitor show 60 Hz?
faq.a2: The system setting is still 60 Hz, the cable or port cannot carry more, battery saver is on, or the window is on another 60 Hz screen.
faq.a3: The time between two frames in milliseconds: 1000 divided by the refresh rate.
faq.q4: Does a higher refresh rate matter outside games?
faq.a4: Scrolling, cursor movement and video look smoother, and fast motion is easier to follow.
faq.a5: No. The frames are counted in your browser tab.

copy.name: How to test a touch screen
copy.blurb: Find dead zones, count how many fingers the screen tracks and check pen pressure. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.title: How to test a touch screen for dead zones and multi-touch
copy.lead: Taps in one part of your screen do nothing, or you want to check a phone or tablet before buying it. You will draw over a grid to find dead zones, count how many fingers the screen tracks and check a pen. Nothing is uploaded.
copy.result: A grid showing every part of the screen that responds, the most fingers tracked at once and whether pressure is reported.
copy.note: A screen protector, wet fingers or a charger with a poor ground can make touch jumpy; test without them if something looks wrong.
copy.s1t: Remove what gets in the way
copy.s1b: Take off thick gloves, dry your fingers and, if touch is erratic, unplug the charger. Clean the screen.
copy.s2t: Open Touch screen test on cv.cm
copy.s2b: The pad shows a grid. Press Full screen to make the pad cover the whole screen so you can reach every edge.
copy.s3b: Draw slow lines across the pad, row by row, to the edges and corners. Every cell you touch fills in; cells that stay empty mark a dead zone.
copy.s4b: Put down as many fingers as you can at once. Touching now shows the count; Most at once keeps the highest. Each finger draws in its own colour.
copy.s5b: Draw with a stylus. Input shows Pen, and Pressure changes as you press harder if the pen reports it.
copy.s6b: Press Clear and test again to confirm a dead zone. If the same cells never respond, it is the screen or digitiser, not the app.
copy.diagram1: Swipe every row: empty cells = dead zone.
copy.diagram2: Phones and tablets: 5–10 fingers · many laptops: 2.

faq.q1: What is a touch screen dead zone?
faq.a1: An area where touches are not detected, often from a damaged digitiser or a cracked screen.
faq.q2: How many touch points does my phone support?
faq.a2: Most phones and tablets track 5–10 fingers. Put down as many as you can and read Most at once.
faq.q3: Why is my touch screen jumpy?
faq.a3: Moisture, a screen protector or a charger without a good ground are common causes. Test again without them.
faq.q4: Can I test it with a mouse?
faq.a4: Yes, hold the left button and draw, but a mouse cannot test multi-touch or dead zones on the screen itself.
faq.a5: No. Touches are drawn in your browser tab only.
